items.description:
The Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC) will launch a fully online attestation service on Jan 1, 2027, allowing students to apply for attestation and download their attested documents without visiting an IBCC office or sending documents by courier.
The decision was taken at a meeting of the IBCC Board of Directors chaired by Executive Director Dr Ghulam Ali Mallah. The service will cover qualifications issued by 29 examination boards across Pakistan, as well as eligible qualifications from madressahs.

items.description:
UN climate talks collapsed on Sunday as the European Union and others rejected a final draft deal put forward by COP31 presidents Turkiye and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.
The failed talks reflect world governments’ struggle this year to muster ambitious action to address the worsening consequences of climate change, as wars, economic pressures and other crises compete for their attention.

items.title: Veteran journalist Husain Naqi passes away in Lahore
items.description:
LAHORE: Veteran journalist and human rights activist Husain Naqi passed away in Lahore on Sunday.
He was a former editor of The News and had also been associated with the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP).
HRCP official Muhammad Ilyas told Dawn that Naqi died of a cardiac arrest.
“He attended a book launch ceremony at the HRCP the previous day. Later, he suffered a heart attack around 6pm on Saturday. He was admitted to a private hospital where he died early in the morning, around 5 am,” Ilyas said, adding that he had left behind three sons.

items.title: Lahore once again ranks as world's most polluted major city as AQI crosses 500
items.description:
Lahore topped the list of the world’s most polluted major cities once again on Sunday morning with an hourly air quality index (AQI) reading of over 500, according to real-time air quality data.
Swiss air quality monitoring platform IQAir’s live global major city ranking placed Lahore first with 538 between 9am and 10am, classifying the quality as ‘hazardous’, indicating extremely polluted conditions and serious health risks for residents.

items.title: Punjab land reforms project reaches 90pc progress
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: The World Bank-fin­a­n­ced Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhan­cement (Pulse) project has achieved 90 per cent physical progress, recording 69.9 million land rights in its information system against a target of 50.7 million, with 31pc registered in women’s names.

items.title: Textile exports rise 6.35pc in July-October
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s textile and clothing exports grew by 6.35 per cent to $6.797 billion in July-October 2026–27, from $6.391bn in the corresponding period last year.
The modest rise in export proceeds was attributed to elevated input costs, which eroded exporters’ competitiveness, and external shocks that disrupted shipments, according to data from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics.

items.title: Journalist’s bail plea rejected
items.description:
QUETTA: A local court in Quetta on Saturday rejected the bail application of Islamabad-based journalist Shahid Maitla.
The bail application was filed by Rahib Buledi Advocate and other lawyers in the court of Judicial Magistrate-VII.
Judicial Magistrate Akhtar Shah, who had reserved the verdict on the application, announced the decision.
Shahid Maitla was arrested under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) on a complaint lodged by former caretaker prime minister Anwarul Haq Kakar. After his arrest, Shahid Maitla was shifted from Islamabad to Quetta.He is currently on judicial remand

items.title: Any talks with India on terrorism must be 'evidence-based', says Musadik Malik
items.description:
Federal minister Musadik Malik said on Sunday that any dialogue between Pakistan and India on terrorism must be “based on evidence”.
Malik is in New Delhi on a three-day trip to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making him the first Pakistani minister to visit the neighbour since former foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari attended an SCO meeting in May 2023.

items.title: Varma century in vain as Pakistan Shaheens down India A in Asia Cup Rising Stars clash
items.description:
Pakistan Shaheens overcame a late challenge from Tilak Varma to beat India A by 48 runs in their Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha on Sunday, defending a total of 313 after bowling out their opponents with five balls to spare.
Skipper Varma struck a century before becoming the last man dismissed for 100 off 149 balls, while Shahbaz Ahmed made 56 in a seventh-wicket stand that briefly revived India’s hopes.

items.title: More than 2,300 Indian Sikh pilgrims arrive in Pakistan to mark Guru Nanak's birthday
items.description:
LAHORE: Over 2,300 Indian Sikh pilgrims arrived in Pakistan through the Wagah Border on Sunday to attend celebrations marking the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism.
The visiting pilgrims were received by Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) Chairman Qamar Zaman, Secretary Nasir Mushtaq, Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee (PSGPC) President and Punjab Minorities Minister Sardar Ramesh Singh Arora, the committee’s secretary general Satwant Kaur and other officials at the Wagah border, where the jatha leaders were presented with bouquets.
